description: The line plot, titled "Performance w.r.t. Temperature," illustrates the relationship between accuracy (measured as Pass@8) and temperature for three different methods: On-policy RL, SFT, and a third method represented by a red star line (likely the proposed method or a baseline). The x-axis, labeled "Temperature," ranges from 0.1 to 1.0 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy (Pass@8)," ranges from 62.5 to 80.0, also on a linear scale, with major gridlines at intervals of 2.5. The On-policy RL method, shown with yellow triangles connected by a solid line, exhibits a sharp increase in accuracy from approximately 64.0 at a temperature of 0.1 to a peak of about 75.0 at 0.8, followed by a decline to around 73.0 at 1.0. The SFT method, represented by teal downward-pointing triangles connected by a solid line, starts at a high accuracy of about 76.0 at a temperature of 0.1 and generally trends downward to approximately 74.0 at 1.0, with a noticeable dip to around 70.0 at a temperature of 0.5. The red star line, corresponding to the third method, begins at a high accuracy of about 76.0, shows a slight initial dip, and then remains relatively stable, fluctuating between approximately 76.0 and 80.0 across the temperature range, with a peak near 80.0 at a temperature of 0.9.
